title: Colorway
content: ### **List of Contents** **Open and Update** **Add** **Edit** **Set Option** **View Mode** **Snapshot** **Switch Colorway** #### **A garment file can be applied in various colors.** **** #### #### **Open and Update** 1. Click the Main Menu » Production » **Colorway (O).** 2. After editing and adjusting the 3D view, click the **Update** button at the top left of the Colorway Editor. #### #### **Add** **Add (Default)** 1. Click the ![Icon Button1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33016678706073) 'Add' button at the top-right corner in Colorway Editor. → By default, a colorway is added based on the selected colorway, allowing only the material properties such as color and texture to be changed. Therefore, a single item (fabric, graphic, trims, etc.) will have different materials for each colorway, and this can be confirmed in the object browser. **![Materials.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33900058646681)** **📝Note:** Even if the Colorway Editor window is closed, you can check the variations for each colorway in the object browser, and you can show or hide them with ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33016752132377) **Show All Colorways** option in the top left corner. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38137431723417) **Add as Custom Settings** For various colorways, you can directly set the variation application range for each item. Refer to the example below and set it at once in the colorway addition step, and easily edit and manage it. 1. Click the ![add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33900118520729) 'Add as Custom Settings' button at the top-right corner in Colorway Editor. → A list of items for the selected colorway appears in the Add Colorway window. ![Add Colorway.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/32988767931801) 2. Directly set the variation application range for each item of the colorway to be added. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Materials** | Based on the item of the selected colorway, only [material properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047317454-Set-Fabric-Materials) such as color and texture can be changed. The same applies as for additional (default) results. _Example) If the physical properties of the fabric and the shape of the button are the same but only the color is different_ ![Materials.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33900058646681) **All Properties** | Items in the selected colorway are automatically copied and applied as new items, allowing all properties to be changed differently. _Example) If it is a completely different fabric or the shape of the button is different._ ![All Properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33900118551833) **Link** | It can be used as the same item as the selected colorway without changing its properties. This option is applied simultaneously when two items are linked to each other and their properties are changed. _Example) When the same fabric and graphics (logo) are used in all colorways_ ![Link.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33900118572697) #### #### **Edit** **Change Properties** 1. Select the thumbnail of the item you want to change in the Colorway Editor window, or select the item in the object browser. → The properties of the item appear in the property editor. 2. Change [material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047317454-Set-Fabric-Textures) properties. 3. Properties other than material can be changed by directly selecting the corresponding item in the object browser. **📝****Note:** After selecting a graphic with Transform Graphic tool, uncheck the '**Property Editor > Link All Colorways > Angle or Position'** option to rotate or position the graphic differently for each colorway. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38137431723417) ## ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45591047474713) ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45590542185369) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/SdzGQ4nxT2o?feature=shared&t=15) Edit the fabric's side and back, along with trims, directly in the Colorway Editor. ![colorway1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45592187269273) ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38137431723417) #### **Assign Items** You can easily and quickly choose whether to apply it to the current colorway only or to all colorways when assigning an item from the Object Browser. 1. Drag and drop an item (fabric, graphics, subsidiary materials, etc.) from Object Browser to the 3D garment. 2. In Assign to Colorway window, specify how an item will be assigned to the colorway by default. _*__This window will appear only the first time. The default setting can be changed in**User Settings » Other » Colorway** option. _ 3. Even with a default setting, the option can still be changed by pressing the **Ctrl** key while dragging and dropping afterward. _**✨Tip:**_ Drag and drop the items from Object Browser, Library or your computer onto the thumbnail in Colorway Editor. It can be applied to the item of that colorway, not all colorways. #### #### **Set Option** 1. Right-click on each colorway or each item's thumbnail in a colorway to set the desired options. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Colorway** | **Delete** | Delete the colorway. **Rename** | Change the name of the colorway. **Item** | **Unlink All Colorways** | Unlink the linked item so that it can have different materials applied to each colorway or apply different properties altogether. **Select All with Same Color** | The same color within the colorway is automatically selected. **Hide Other Graphics** | You can quickly hide multiple graphics at once. Hide all other graphics that use the same item as the selected graphic. ![Colorway_hide graphics.gif](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38214025050777) #### #### **View Mode** 1. Click the **Show Details** button at the bottom-right corner. → Colorway window switches to "Viewer Mode" where you can see the colorway thumbnails only. 2. Size thumbnails by controlling the scroll bar at the bottom-left corner, or arrange the thumbnails in single or multiple lines by clicking the arrangement button. #### #### **Snapshot** 1. Click on the **Save Image** button at the left-top corner. 2. Select either a snapshot of the 3D garments for all colorways, or the Colorway Editor showing all items used per colorway. ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48746065495449) When saving a snapshot of the Colorway Editor, you can select the image scale (1x, 2x, 3x, 4x) to define the resolution of the saved file. Higher values produce larger and sharper images. #### #### **Switch Colorway** Quickly switch the current colorway by clicking color chips in the Object Browser. ![Colorway.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45591047477273) **📝Note:** If you save the garment with colorway as a project file in version 2024.1, it may not be compatible properly with lower versions (2024.0, 7.3). Therefore, if necessary, it is recommended to separately save the project file for colorway compatibility through the '**Main Menu > File > Save As > Project (with Other Files) menu**' option. #### **Go back to the List of Contents**

title: CLO to Twinmotion: FBX Workflow
content: ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52177334258201) ## ## **Objective** This guide explains how to prepare avatars and garments in your CLO project for a seamless import into Twinmotion using the correct FBX export settings. ## **Operation** There are two primary methods for importing CLO avatars and garments into Twinmotion. For either method, you can use CLO's [**Import/Export Option Preset feature**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/48665693640985-Import-Export-Option-Preset#h_01JZS3ZC16E38XAFDDSED8CDDA)**** to save your export settings, which will help streamline the export process. ### **Preserving CLO Fabric Materials in Twinmotion** This process ensures that fabric textures and details created in CLO are accurately transferred to Twinmotion. Upon import, each fabric from your CLO project will become a separate material in Twinmotion, which will require texture relinking. #### **Step 1: Bake and Export UV Maps from CLO** In CLO's UV Editor, bake and export all necessary texture maps for your garments (e.g., Diffuse, Normal, Roughness). #### **Step 2: Configure FBX Export Settings** Export the project as an FBX file using the following specific settings: * Unified UV Coordinates * Single Object * Thick (for geometry) * Scale: cm * Embed Media #### **Step 3: Relink Texture Maps in Twinmotion** After importing the FBX into Twinmotion, select one of the new materials derived from a CLO fabric. Manually relink the exported texture maps (from Step 1) to their corresponding channels in the Twinmotion material editor. #### **Step 4: Apply the Corrected Material** Once one material is correctly configured, use the material picker tool to apply this corrected material to all other surfaces that share the same fabric. **Note** : For higher fidelity, ensure that details like seamlines and puckering are included in the normal map you bake from CLO. This helps create a final render in Twinmotion that is more consistent with the original CLO design. ### **Applying New Materials in Twinmotion** This workflow is optimized for situations where you plan to replace the original CLO fabrics with new materials from the Twinmotion library. By exporting without unified UVs, you ensure that textures map cleanly across individual pattern pieces, which is ideal for applying tiling materials. #### **Step 1: Configure FBX Export Settings** Export the project as an FBX file from CLO with the following specific settings: * Unified UV Coordinates: Unchecked * Single Object * Thick (for geometry) * Scale: cm * Embed Media * Diffuse Color Combined on Texture #### **Step 2: Apply Materials in Twinmotion** Upon importing the FBX, Twinmotion will automatically group the geometry based on the materials assigned in CLO. * Behavior: All pattern pieces that shared the same fabric in CLO (e.g., "Cotton Twill") will now be treated as a single material surface in Twinmotion. * Action: Simply drag and drop a new Twinmotion material onto any part of that surface. It will instantly update all associated pattern pieces at once. **Note** : This method will not preserve Normal Maps for fine details like seamlines or puckering. However, the trade-off is superior texture mapping at the seams and edges of each pattern piece, preventing texture distortion when applying new materials in Twinmotion.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for preparing avatars and garments in CLO for seamless import into Twinmotion, outlining the essential steps and settings needed to ensure accurate material transfer and optimal rendering.

title: Offset as Internal Line
content: **List of Contents** Offset as Internal Line Distribute Internal Line between Segments Create a new Internal line at regular intervals along the pattern outline or Internal line of the pattern. #### **Offset as Internal Line** 1. Click on ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48676347350553) **Edit Pattern** or**![Transform Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48676369859353) Transform Pattern** in the 2D toolbar. 2. Right-click on the pattern outline or internal line and click **Offset as Internal Line**. → Offset as Internal Line option window appears. 3. Set detailed options. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Number of Offsets** | Enter the number to be created. **Distance** | Enter the distance from the selected segment. **All** | Set the distance of all segments to be the same . **Individual** | Set the spacing for each line segment individually. **Offset From** | When inputting individual distances, the individual line can be set as the previous or selected line. **Reverse Direction** | Change in the reverse direction of the selected segment. **Both Sides** | Create internal lines in both directions based on the selected segment. **Extend** | **to Pattern Outline** | Extend to Pattern Outline of the pattern. **to Internal Line** | Extend to Pattern Outline or Internal Line of the pattern. 4. Click **OK**. → Depending on the settings, the internal line/shape is created. → If it is a curve, the curve point is automatically optimized. #### **Distribute Internal Line between Segment** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Select the two internal lines or pattern outlines that will be the basis for the internal lines creating. **📝Note:****** If the outline or Internal line of the pattern is divided into multiple points, press the Shift key on the keyboard to select them all. 3. Right-click on the selected outline ▶Select **Distribute Internal Line between Segment.** → The internal line option window appears along the slope. 4. Set the following options arbitrarily and click OK. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Number of Offsets** | Set the number of internal lines to be created. **Offset** | Set the spacing between the internal lines to be created. **Distnace to Segement Edge** | Set the spacing of the internal lines to be created away from the outline. **Reverse Direction** | Changes the set internal left and right. **Opposite Segment** | Changes the set internal up and down. **Straight Line** | Create an internal line as a straight line. **Perpendicular Direction** | Create an internal line in the vertical direction of the selected outline. **Graduate Segment Lengths** | The internal line does not extend to the pattern outline but fits into an imaginary line that connects the two selected line points in a straight line. **Extend to Unfolded Line** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48676369860633) Extend an internal line to the unfolded line on a half-symmetrical pattern. → An internal line is created based on the setting of each option. #### Go back to the List of Contents

title: I have a verification issue. What should I do?
content: **Question** I have a verification issue. What should I do? **Answer** Please use Chrome instead of other internet browsers. CLO website is optimized as Chrome. [CASE 1] If you didn't receive the verification email, please check your spam mailbox. Sometimes the verification email can be found in your spam folder, or you will need to refresh your browser. [CASE 2] If CLO web requires verification, even if you already verify it, please remove your old cookie and cache. **In Chrome** 1. On your computer, open Chrome. 2. At the top right, click More. 3. Click More tools. Clear browsing data. 4. At the top, choose a time range. To **delete** everything, select All time. 5. Next to "**Cookies** and other site data" and "**Cached** images and files," check the boxes. 6. Click Clear data. [CASE 3] Some school domains block external emails. If so, you can check your school domain is connected to the verification email on [Verify Email Address Link](https://www.verifyemailaddress.org/). If you see the result as "Connecting did not work", please ask your school admin (especially the technical division) to check if you could receive the verification email from the domain "[clo-set.com](mailto:noreply@clo-set.com)". If you still have not received your verification email, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus)[.](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus)
content_description: This web page provides troubleshooting steps for resolving verification issues with the CLO website, emphasizing the use of Chrome and offering solutions for common problems.

content: **Question** Can I import 3D body scan data into CLO? **Answer** Yes, 3D body scans can be imported into CLO as long as they are in OBJ or FBX file format. However, the body mesh has to be "cleaned" (no holes or noises) so that garments can be fitted correctly.

title: Garment Animation Making
content: **Objective** Tips for creating stable and realistic garment animation for multi-layered garments. ** Operation** **Optimize 3D Garment for Animation** The heavier the garment, the slower and harder it records. Follow the steps below to make it lighter. 1. For a multi-layered garment, increase particle distance to 20mm for inner layers that are not as visible as outer layers. 2. Delete invisible and any other unnecessary layers. 3. Outer layers: →Set the particle distance to 10mm for parts that does not require higher level of expression of wrinkles. →Set the particle distance to 5mm for parts that require higher level of expression of wrinkles. If there is large quantity of layers set to 5mm, set all of them to 7mm. ****Fix Garment**** If garment is not fixed to avatar while recording the animation, the garment moves drastically around the avatar due to collision. Certain parts of the garment need to be fixed to the avatar or itself to create more realistic recording. →Use functions such as 'Avatar Tape' or 'Tack on Avatar' to attach shoulder and sides of the garment. →Use 'Tack' function for overlapped layers or any parts that may dangle. **Increase Transition Animation Time** Increase the transition animation time for heavier garments. In the animation dialogue, enter 5FPS to stabilize the simulation. This makes the avatar movement slower which helps to minimize the collision between the garments. **Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for the First Recording** Setting Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' minimizes the collision between the avatar and garments. To save time, the simulation quality can be set to 'Normal' for the middle part of the recording as the avatar and garments tend to collide more in the beginning and end. Make sure the simulation to set the quality back on 'Complete' for the end of the Transition Animation. **Reevaluate Draping of the Garment after the Recording** As the avatar moves, some parts of the garment may collide. When the simulation is off, the 3D garment may appear fine, however there is possibility of unnoticeable collision which may destabilize rest of the recording. →Return to Simulation Mode. **※ Note:** From ver2.5.0, it is possible to simulate by pressing the **Simulation** button without recording it. →Active simulation and make sure the entire garment simulation is stable. →If any parts of the garment is unstable, readjust the layers by using the **Select/Move** tool. →Once the simulation has been stabilized, go back to the Animation Mode. **Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' when Recording the Actual Garment Animation ** Make sure to set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for final recordings of Garment Animation as the 'Complete' and the 'Normal' give clearly different results in expressing reality.
content_description: This webpage provides essential tips for optimizing and stabilizing the animation of multi-layered garments, ensuring realistic draping and movement.

title: Arrange Pattern with Arrangement Points/Flip Wrap Direction
content: **Objective** Arrangement Points are created on the basis of the Bounding Volume surrounding the Avatar, and are arranged on the Avatar according to the Bounding Volume's curves. **※ Note:** Precise arrangement is available by using [Gizmo](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002802728) or [Property Editor](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004877468) even after arranging with Arrangement Points. **Location** Avatar Display ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005508288/AVT_03Points_Off.png) **Show Arrangement Points** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Avatar Display ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005508288/AVT_03Points_Off.png) **Show Arrangement Points** → The Arrangement Points appear around the Avatar. 2. Select a Pattern and hover the mouse over an Arrangement Point. → A preview of the Pattern placement is being displayed (ver2.4.0). 3. Select a desired Arrangement Point. → The center of the Pattern is now being placed according to the selected Arrangement Point. → Symmetric Arrangement occurs as long as the Patterns and Arrangement Points have symmetry applied (ver3.0.0). **※ Note:** **Flip Wrap Direction** Patterns that the length are longer than the Bounding Volume, such as cuffs, get arranged spiral. Right-click on patterns in the 3D window ▶ Click **Flip Wrap Direction** to flip its direction.** **

title: Edit V-Ray Camera Properties
content: #### **Create a dynamic image for 3D garments with enhanced camera settings replicated from real-world film/DSLR/video cameras: ISO, f-number, effects, and more. ** **Location** The ![Camera Properties On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44250068287897)**Camera Properties** can be accessed through several paths: \- Main Menu ▶ Render ▶ Render ▶ Render window toolbar ▶ **Camera Properties** \- Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Preferences ▶ Camera Properties ▶ **Default Camera** \- Object Browser ▶ Scene tab ▶ Environment ▶ Camera ▶ **Default Camera** \- right-click pop-up menu in 3D window ▶ Camera Properties ▶ **Default Camera** **Lens** **Default/Panorama (Render Only):** Select a view type between default and panorama. **Field of View:** Sets a view range by adjusting the camera lens's field of view. **View Orientation** **Type:** Select a view type between Spherical (object-centered) or Absolute (X-, Y-centered). **Spherical** **Distance:** Zooms in and out. **Horizontal Angle:** Rotates the camera view horizontally. **Vertical Angle:** Rotates the camera view vertically. **Absolute** **Horizontal Angle:** Pans the camera view horizontally. **Vertical Angle:** Pans the camera view vertically. **Clipping Plane** **Near:** Assigns the nearest distance that the camera can capture. **Far:** Assigns the farthest distance that the camera can capture. **Physical Camera** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Exposure** | Configure the amount of light penetrating into the camera to change the brightness. To do so effectively, use the **Exposure** option instead of adjusting the brightness of the **[V-Ray Lights](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899168-Edit-V-Ray-Light-Properties)**. **ISO** | Adjust the sensitivity of the film. A small value results in a darker image; a high value in a brighter one. ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360016901473) **F-Number** | Adjust the openness of the aperture. A high value results in a darker image; a small value in a brighter one. ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360016147354) **Shutter Speed (1/s)** | Adjust the shutter speed with the unit of 1/s. When the shutter speed is 1/30s, the shutter is open for one-thirtieth of a second. To replicate the same effect, you should type in 30. The amount of the penetrating light decreases with an increased number of shutter blinks. Therefore, a high value results in a darker image; a small value in a brighter one. ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360016147414) **Depth of Field** | Configure the depth of field by adjusting the camera's focus. The depth of field is dependent on both the **Focus Distance** and the **F-Number**. **Viewpoint Focus** | ## ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44250068288665) ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/50223447482521)[ Watch Video](https://youtu.be/iflI4v36pi4?feature=shared&t=455) Each [**Custom View**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004420828-Custom-View) can be rendered with an individually set Depth of Field. 1\. Enter the desired Focus Distance value in the Custom Views fields. 2\. Or, adjust the Focus Distance directly during Interactive Render to automatically apply the value by adding a new view or overwriting an existing view in the Custom View window. ** Focus Distance ** | Set the camera's focus point as needed. Use the **F-Number** option to adjust the focus length (clear area), starting from the focus point. A larger **F-Number** results in a larger clear area is; a smaller number in a narrower one. As adjusting the focus length with the **Focus Distance** is not intuitive, using the **Focus by Left Click** option is recommended. ** Focus by Left Click ** | Click to set the focus point. When the focus point is selected, the Focus Distance is calculated automatically. ** Effects ** | Stretch the image either vertically or horizontally.
content_description: Discover how to create dynamic 3D garment images by utilizing advanced camera settings—such as ISO, f-number, and effects—replicating the capabilities of real-world film and DSLR cameras.

title: Rendering Thickness
content: **** Set the rendering thickness for the patterns. Rendering thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. **** 1. Select the pattern to set the rendering thickness. _* To see the rendering thickness,[3D Garment Rendering](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001025968-3D-Window-Display-Icons#Click3) Style must be set to one of the thick-surface styles. _ 2. Set the thickness options in Property Editor. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Add'l Thickness - Rendering** | Enter desired rendering thickness value. This value is for rendering purposes only and does not affect collisions. However, when exporting, enabling the Thick option will export both the Side and Back Mesh and UVs **✨Tip:** Collision thickness can be adjusted at [Simation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness - Collision]. **Extrusion Direction** | Specify the direction in which thickness is applied based on the Pattern Plane. **Both** | Apply thickness evenly to both the front and back based on the Pattern. **Forward** | Apply thickness forward. **Backward** | Apply thickness backward. Toggle each side on or off to determine whether to generate the Mesh. **Front Face** | Specify whether to generate the Front Face. **Back Face** | Specify whether to generate the Back Face. **Seam Face** | Specify whether to generate the surface where the stitched and bonded parts meet. **Side Geometry** | **Curvature (%)** | Specify the curvature. **Resolution** | Set the number of subdivisions. **Doubled Sided** | Apply the same curve to both sides. **UV Expansion**** **** **| ## ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45512137895065) **![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777)**[Watch Video](https://youtu.be/iflI4v36pi4?feature=shared&t=401) The side and back UVs can be edited in [UV Editor](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053418574-UV-Editor-Mode). **Back Face** | Switch the UV from the front to the back. **Side Face** | Expand the UVs to include the side.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for setting rendering thickness for fabric patterns in 3D garment rendering, including options for extrusion direction, mesh generation, and UV editing.

title: How to uninstall CLO completely
content: In the process of Live Update or alternately using multiple CLO versions, various files and settings that make up the CLO software may be damaged, causing the CLO software to not operate normally. You can solve this problem by completely uninstalling the CLO software and configuration files and then reinstalling with the latest CLO installer. **Note** * Only the files and settings that make up the CLO software are deleted, and user-created files are remain. * Before uninstalling the CLO software, please back up your working files to a safe place. * If you have changed the CLO install path, find the path and delete it. * * * **Windows** **1 Logging out of CLO Software or deactivating from website** * Under the CLO Settings menu, select Logout or Deactivate License. * [Deactivate CLO from website](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500000942261) **2 Uninstall CLO software** * Go to Windows Start > Settings > Apps or Installed Apps > CLO Software and click Uninstall. * If you have installed different product types or multiple versions, uninstall all CLO software using the above method. ![001_Win_Uninstall.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/16260393832729) **3 Delete Registry** * Windows Search > Type _'Registry Editor'_ > open as administrator > delete the CLO registry. * Path: _Computer\HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\CLO Virtual Fashion_ * If you don't see the CLO product name in the Windows Registry, all have been deleted. * Note that deleting the CLO product key from the Windows Registry will make CLO behave as if it was installed for the first time. If you want to completely reset user settings of the CLO software, you can use the method of deleting only the registry keys of CLO. ![007_Delete_CLO_Registry_Keys.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49131892784665) **4 Delete CLO install folder and Assets folder** * Even after deleting the program, additional downloaded files and some configurations may remain. * The default install path is C:\Program Files\CLO{product name}, select and delete the entire CLO folder. **5 Delete CLO Assets folder from Windows shared folder** * The default install path is C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO, select and delete the entire CLO folder. **6 Delete hidden CLO files** * Some CLO configuration files are stored as hidden files. * Go to Windows File Explorer > Options > Folder Options. * Select 'Show hidden files' as shown below and click the 'Apply to Folders' button. ![007_Folder_option.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/16264058474777) * Go to C:\Users\\{Windows user name}\AppData\Local, select the CLO folder and delete it. ![005_hidden.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/16263600237849) * * * **Mac** Note: before uninstalling the CLO software, please back up your working files to a safe place. **1 Logging out of CLO Software or deactivating from website** * From the SETTINGS Menu, Log Out or Deactivate License of CLO. The application will Quit. * [Deactivate CLO from website >](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500000942261) **2 Uninstall CLO software** * Open the MAIN APPLICATION folder on your computer. NOT the Application folder in the User Folder. * Find the CLO, Right-Click & Move to Trash. Only do this if you want to fully uninstall CLO. ![008_macOS_uninstall.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/16557180465689) **3 Delete CLO Assets folder** * To remove all the CLO Assets, go into your DOCUMENTS Folder. Delete the CLO Folder there. ![009_macOS_assets.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/16557381041177) **4 Delete hidden CLO files** * Go to your HOME Folder, use Column & navigate to the Go Menu. Note the contents on the menu and in the items in the Home folder. Release the menu. ![009_macOS_Home.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/16558744414617) * Type SHIFT + COMMAND + PERIOD (.) this will activate hidden items. * A few things will show up in the Applications folder. Return to the Go Menu and note that “LIBRARY” is now visible and there are more Items available in the Home folder. Some are dimmed. These are items that are normally hidden. * Go into the LIBRARY folder and delete the CLO folder under the APPLICATION SUPPORT folder. ![010_macOS_Libarary.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/16558775926553) * Next, still in the Library, go into Preferences. * Select all the files that begin with COM.CLO. (The full name will differ depending on which version of the software you downloaded and installed). * Right-Click on one of the selected files and Move to Trash. * Empty your Trash. ![011_macOS_hidden.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/16558970688025) **Note** * If you have deleted only the CLO Preferences files, when you start CLO again it will be as if it is opening for the first time; you will need to input your login information, add your Favorites to the Library and customize your User Settings.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for completely uninstalling and reinstalling the CLO software to resolve issues stemming from damaged files and settings.

title: Record Animation
content: **Objective** Record garment animation. **※ Note: **Follow the link; [Process of Making Garment Animation](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000560428) for your reference on creating garment animation in details. ** Location** Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005706147/ani_02rec_none.png) **Record** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005706147/ani_02rec_none.png) **Record** → Simulation turns on automatically and it is now being recorded in frames. → If a Transition Animation is created, the recording automatically stops at the end of the Transition Animation frame and starts again (ver2.5.0). **※ Note: **Transition Animation is auto-generated animation tool which automatically generates for stabilizing transition when the original Avatar pose is different to the first pose in the motion file. Once the garment and avatar arrive in a new position, it is no longer in need therefore the recording automatically stops for you to delete this unnecessary part. 2. Once the Avatar's motion ends, the recording automatically stops. To stop the recording while it is in process, click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005758308/ani_btn_stop_over.png) **Pause** button.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for recording garment animations using the Animation Editor in CLO 3D, including tips on managing transitions and stopping recordings.

title: Play Animation
content: **Objective** Play the recorded garment animation. **Location** Animation Mode ▶ **Animation Editor Upper Toolbar** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005763588/Aimation_mode_editor_window_en__1_.PNG) **※ Note** **Edit Animation Tools** (Start) | Moves to the beginning of the play area. ---|--- ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005710867/ani_btn_play_none.png) (Play) | Plays the play area. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005763568/ani_btn_stop_over.png) (Pause) | Pauses temporarily on the play area. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005710887/ani_btn_right_double_none.png) (End) | Moves to the end of the play area. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005763528/ani_btn_re_none.png) (Repeat) | Repeats the play area. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005710927/ani_btn_1x_none.png) (1x) | Changes the play speed. (1/4x, 1/2x, 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005763488/04_Frame_Stepping.png) (Frame Stepping /Real Time) | Changes the play unit in frames or seconds. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005710847/07.png) | Set the first frame to be played. (Click-and-drag on the timeline also allows to set the first frame.) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005763508/06.png) | Set the last frame to be played. (Click-and-drag on the timeline also allows to set the first frame.) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005763548/Animation_____.png)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive overview of the Animation Mode tools in the Animation Editor, enabling users to play, pause, and manipulate recorded garment animations efficiently.

title: How to Speed Up CLO
content: In this article, learn how to improve the performance of your CLO software and keep it optimal. The overall performance of CLO is affected by computer specifications, maintenance, and the number of programs running, but it also varies depending on user settings and garment file properties within the software. Problem Situations ![001_Windows.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36782529045401) * CLO software becomes unresponsive or quits unexpectedly. * It takes a long time to open the file. * It takes a long time to save the file you worked on. * Simulation slows down or quits unexpectedly. * Rendering freezes or quits unexpectedly. * * * Show Frame Rate ![001_FPS.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49482274897561) * **Go to the top menu > Settings > Display > Environment > Show Frame Rate**, and you will see several numbers in the lower left corner of the 3D window, including FPS (Frames Per Second), which shows real-time results of the simulation speed of your garment and the overall performance of your computer. * The screenshot above is the result of putting a halter-neck dress on a CLO avatar, adjusting the particle distance to 10, and simulating in Normal-CPU mode. It consists of 6 patterns, 0 trims, 20 sewing lines, 15261 vertices, and shows a speed of about 52fps in Normal (Default) simulation. * Each user's perceived performance is different, and it is advantageous to do actual garment editing and design work under high frame rate conditions. * * * User Settings ![002_AA.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49482274910873) * **Graphic Options > Antialiasing**: For low-end computers with only Intel Graphics as well as Macs with integrated memory of 8GB or less, set the Antialiasing value to x8 or lower. The higher the anti-aliasing setting, the smoother the images and videos that eliminate jaggies will be, but more video memory and high-performance graphics processing will be required. * **Normal Blending, Default Rendering, Image Resolution Setting** : These are options that determine the various methods and modes for configuring graphics, images, textures, and screens, and the CLO team recommends using them in their default unless there is a special purpose. * Please note that starting with CLO 2024.2, the VBO setting has been removed and integrated into the CLO software as _"**VBO_enabled**."_ VBO allows you to store vertex data in GPU memory, enabling fast 3D rendering. All modern GPUs support this, so users do not need to manually turn it on or off. ![004_Auto_Save.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36782529053337) * **Default Files > Auto Save > Time Interval (min**): Starting with CLO v6.1, it is set to 10 minutes by default. If you set this value as low as 1 or 2 minutes, file writing may occur frequently, slowing down CLO's speed. * * * File Properties ![005_ParticleDistance.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36782512763673) * **Particle Distance; default setting 20** * Lower particle distance allows for more realistic garment expressions, but the number of vertices that make up 2D patterns and 3D garments increases dramatically. As a result, the amount of calculations that need to be done on a computer can increase by several to tens of times, which in turn slows down simulation and garment editing. * Rather than setting the particle distance low from the beginning and then creating the garment, it may be more efficient to lower the particle distance after the design stage. ![006_topstitches.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36782512764569) * **Excessive use of OBJ topstitching; change to type "texture"** * OBJ topstitching is a method of dividing the mesh of narrow and long areas into finer pieces than the mesh of regular patterns. Therefore, if you use a lot of OBJ topstitching, the amount of mesh calculation increases and CLO's speed may slow down. * For faster work, it is advantageous to use OBJ topstitches only on the areas where it's absolutely necessary and apply texture-type topstitches to the remaining areas. ![004_animation.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49482337576601) * **Project file containing animation** * In the case of project files containing animation recordings or files containing motion created in other programs, the file size can be several to tens of times larger than a typical CLO project file. So it may take longer to read, edit, and save files. In particular, files containing animation and motion have a file structure that is relatively easy to damage, so handle them with care. ![008_Avatar.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36782529061273) ![007_Trim.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36782512766617) * **Project file containing custom avatars or heavy OBJ trims** * The two pictures above are examples showing the mesh count of the custom avatar's hair and of the trim attached to the garment. * The software is optimized for avatars provided by CLO. If your project file contains heavy custom avatars or heavy OBJ or FBX objects, it may run slowly. * If you're experiencing slow behavior when opening and working with certain project files, check to see if they contain custom avatars or heavy trim objects. * **Ultra-high resolution image files** * When using ultra-high-resolution textures and graphic images to create and express realistic 3D garments, more computer processing and file input/output are required. This leads to performance and speed issues: * When using image files larger than 4000x4000 pixels as textures or graphics images, you may experience speed issues on and in certain computers and CLO usage scenarios. If speed problems occur due to the texture or graphic image you are trying to use, lower the resolution of the images. * **Export files at high resolution** * In file export scenarios, including VRAY rendering, setting the target resolution too high can cause CLO to become very slow or freeze. * In the case of VRAY render, increasing the resolution increases rendering time, and in some cases, rendering may stop due to insufficient video memory. Start with a small image size and default resolution and gradually increase the size to find the optimal render settings for your computer. * When using features such as PDF export and 2D snapshot export, we recommend the default setting of 127 ppi. If it exceeds 200 ppi, both image size and file size may increase tremendously, and file saving may fail in the PDF file format. * **Project file created in an old CLO version** * Due to a flaw in certain versions of CLO software, project files created in those versions may experience speed issues when opened in newer versions. Re-saving in the latest version may resolve these issues. * * * Simulation Modes ![003_Simulation.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49482337579417) * **Normal (Default)** * This is the basic simulation mode for most cases. * **Fitting (Accurate Fabric)** * This feature is designed to produce extremely precise and accurate clothing simulation results. It performs at least 5 times more calculations than the Normal simulation, so it runs slower. * **Animation (Stable)** * This is a preset optimized for garment animation recording. While other simulation modes focus on representing a stationary avatar and the clothes worn on it, this one is designed to simulate the natural movement of clothes following the motion of the moving avatar without losing the sophistication that can be relatively lacking. * **CPU vs. GPU** * CPU simulation is the default and works well for all garments and use scenarios. * GPU simulation is only enabled on Windows computers which equipped Nvidia graphics card, and although there are differences depending on the garment and its properties, it is up to 20 times faster than the CPU-based simulations. When tested on commonly used project files, it is approximately 2 to 5 times faster. ![005_animation_split.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49482274914713) * **Animation Recording** * CLO's animation recording simulates garments that change slightly at each frame and saves the results as a file. Therefore, the CPU-GPU simulation principle described previously is applied as is. You can change animation recording presets and various properties, for high quality animation, use the default 'Animation (Stable)'. * The more flashy and heavy the garment is, and the more total frames of animation there are, the larger the animation data generated, the more hardware resources are required. If you need to record a very long and complex animation, it may be advantageous to record the entire scene by splitting it into about 100 frames as shown above. * * * See also * [CLO System Requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168) * [Visual C++ Redistributable download (Windows only)](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000730068) * [Graphics card problems and troubleshooting](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768) * [Install CLO with administrator privileges](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/17074279996697) * [How to prevent CLO File corruption](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/23206278838681) * Internet speed has little to do with CLO performance. CLO software connects to the internet only when logging in, logging out, downloading assets, uploading and downloading CLO-SET files, and delivering crash logs to the CLO server when a crash occurs. * Computers are sensitive to heat, so if the CPU and GPU temperatures are too high, the computer will not perform properly. To maintain optimal computer performance, periodic cooler cleaning and maintenance are required. If you are unfamiliar with these tasks, contact your company's IT department. * If you are using a laptop, we recommend that you connect the power cable to maintain maximum performance. If the laptop is running on battery mode, it may drop to 1/4 of the maximum performance.
content_description: Discover effective strategies to enhance the performance of your CLO software, addressing key factors like computer specifications, user settings, and garment file properties for an optimal design experience.
